So, next weekend: Copenhagen or Oslo?
I think Copenhagen. It is warmer than Oslo in May.
That's true. But Oslo is more beautiful. The mountains, the fjords...
Maybe. But Oslo is more expensive. A coffee there is twice the price.
OK, that's a good point. And Copenhagen is livelier at night.
Yes. Now the hotel. The Harbor or the Garden?
The Harbor is bigger and more modern. I love the view of the water.
But it is farther from the center. Twenty minutes by bus.
Hmm. And the Garden is seventy euros cheaper.
And cozier. Small hotels are friendlier, too.
OK, you win. The Garden Hotel. But next time, Oslo!
Deal. I'll book it tonight.

I lived in Lisbon for two years, and now I live in Berlin. People always ask me: which city is better? Well, Lisbon is warmer and sunnier, of course. Berlin is colder, but it is bigger and more modern. Lisbon is cheaper, and the food is better. Sorry, Berlin! But Berlin is quieter at night, and the trains are faster. And the people? In Lisbon they are friendlier on the street. In Berlin they are more direct. My answer? Lisbon is more beautiful, but Berlin is easier for my work. So I'll stay here, for now.

This week I stayed in two hotels in Copenhagen. The first one, the Harbor Hotel, was bigger and more modern. The rooms were cleaner, and the view of the water was better. But it was more expensive, and it was farther from the center, twenty minutes by bus. The second one, the Garden Hotel, was smaller and older. But it was cozier, and the people at the desk were friendlier. It was also cheaper, and closer to the restaurants. My choice for next time? The Garden Hotel. Smaller, but happier.

Copenhagen is warmer than Oslo in May. The Garden Hotel is cheaper than the Harbor Hotel. The Harbor Hotel is more modern, but it is farther from the center. The Garden Hotel is cozier and friendlier. So we'll stay at the Garden Hotel.
